title: Where wast thou (Job 38–42)
hook: God answers from the whirlwind with the stars, the sea and the wild ass

segments.voice: Yesterday, ha-satan struck, and Job's three friends sat beside him in silence for seven days. Your line was they sat with him.

Thirty-five chapters of argument. The friends say Job must have sinned. Job says he hasn't, and he wants God to show up and answer the charge, like a man taking his case to court. Let the Almighty answer me, he says, near the end of his speeches. Then the long poem stops, and the Douay-Rheims says: "Then the Lord answered Job out of a whirlwind." And everyone reading for the first time leans in, because now, surely, the why will come.
screen: `THIRTY-FIVE CHAPTERS OF ARGUMENT.` → `LET THE ALMIGHTY ANSWER ME.` → `GOD SPEAKS OUT OF A STORM.`

segments.voice: It doesn't. God answers Job with questions of his own, and the first is today's title: "Where wast thou" when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell me, if you understand. Who set its measures? Who shut up the sea behind doors when it burst out of the womb, and said: this far, and no farther? Have you commanded the morning, walked in the depths of the sea, or seen the storehouses of the snow? Can you join together the shining Pleiades, or stop Arcturus turning? Who feeds the young ravens when they cry? Who set the wild ass free, to laugh at the noise of the city? It goes on for four chapters: the ostrich, the war horse, the hawk, and two huge creatures, Behemoth and Leviathan. God never mentions the wager from chapter one, and never says why Job suffered. Instead he walks Job through a world far bigger and wilder than his question, most of it nothing to do with people at all. And Job is answered. Not with an explanation, but with a presence. He says, roughly: I had heard of you with my ears, but now my eye sees you. Then two surprises. God tells the friends they did not speak rightly about him, as Job did, the Job who argued and complained. And Job's fortunes are restored, and he gives his three daughters an inheritance alongside their brothers, which was rare. The Hebrew names them Jemimah, Keziah and Keren-happuch. Jerome translated the names into Latin, so the Douay calls them Dies, Cassia and Cornustibii: Day, Cinnamon, and a horn of eye paint.
screen: `QUESTIONS ANSWERED WITH QUESTIONS.` · `THE PLEIADES, THE RAVENS, THE WILD ASS.` · `NO EXPLANATION, BUT A PRESENCE.` · `NOW MY EYE SEES THEE.` · then, large: `WHERE WAST THOU?`

segments.voice: Step outside if you can, or stand at a window, and let your eyes go as far as they can: clouds, a tree, the light. Hold one unanswered why up against the size of what you're looking at; the ravens are being fed somewhere right now. If you pray, simply be in God's presence, as Job was, without an answer.
Leviathan. One of the two huge creatures God points to near the end of his answer to Job, a world wilder than any question Job asked. Today's word.
Your line: the whirlwind answered. Job heard of God, and then he saw. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics hear God's speech from the whirlwind at Sunday Mass in one year of the cycle, paired with the Gospel of Jesus calming the storm, and the Book of Job is read at weekday Mass for a week in autumn of one year of the weekday cycle.
